messages.content: Explain why the Moon appears to go through phases. Answer in two to four sentences of plain prose.

message.content: The Moon appears to go through phases because it orbits the Earth, which constantly changes our viewing angle of its sunlit side. While the Sun always illuminates exactly half of the Moon, the amount of that lit portion we can see from Earth changes as the Moon moves. Consequently, we see different fractions of the bright side over the course of a month, creating the appearance of changing shapes.
